pull_requests.title: Add pull request intake for StatArena data contributions
pull_requests.body:
## What this adds

- A public Contribute data page with two routes: Simulated DGP and Real-data problem. Each route has a Markdown template and a filled JASA example with a DAG, estimand and reproducibility details.
- One proposal per GitHub pull request, a PR checklist, and a reviewer guide. Private evaluation or restricted materials are handled separately with a maintainer.
- An automated structural check for new submissions and scoped CODEOWNERS for review routing. The fork check reads the proposed Markdown from GitHub using the trusted base revision. The rollout PR runs the validator's self-tests.

## Validation

- Exercised the homepage and both template links in Chromium at desktop and mobile widths.
- Ran 10 validator unit tests. Both completed examples pass, while the unfilled templates and invalid fixtures are rejected.
- Ran the R snippets for both examples using the public source material and checked the reported outputs.
- Matched the existing site regression expectations to the current homepage and IV baseline.

Public Pages deployment follows maintainer review and merge.

## StatArena data contribution

**Track** · Simulated DGP

**Case file** · `data-submissions/simulated-dgp/submissions/proximal-linear-bridge.md`

**Summary** · A literature-based proximal linear-bridge scenario with latent confounding, observable proxies and an analytic constant CATE reference. This is a contribution/reviewer workflow pilot for a mechanism already represented in the earlier internal collection, not a claim of a new catalog mechanism or new model scores.

- [ ] This PR adds or updates one case under the corresponding track's `submissions/` directory.
- [ ] The case follows the track template and describes its assumptions, data source and evaluation target.
- [ ] I checked what can be shared in this public PR and kept restricted materials in the agreed private review channel.

pull_requests.title: datasubmission test
pull_requests.body:
This PR adds a simulation proposal for estimating pointwise CATE when treatment effects are strongly localized despite a simple marginal outcome regression. Opposite-signed Gaussian bumps in the treatment-arm means create heterogeneous effects that disappear when the arms are averaged.

The mechanism comes from Section 5.2 of Rolling and Yang (2014), *Model selection for estimating treatment effects*, **JRSS-B**, 76(4), 749–769. Public sources: [[paper DOI](https://doi.org/10.1111/rssb.12043)](https://doi.org/10.1111/rssb.12043) and [[publisher article](https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/article/76/4/749/7076033)](https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/article/76/4/749/7076033). Selecting a fixed CATE query and implementing the collection interface are documented adaptations.

Methods receive the baseline effect modifier `U`, randomized treatment `A`, continuous outcome `Y` and the same query metadata.

```mermaid
graph LR
    U["Pretreatment effect modifier U"] --> Y["Outcome Y"]
    A["Randomized treatment A"] --> Y
```

Identification assumes independent individuals, consistency, no interference, randomized assignment and positivity. The target is the conditional treatment-versus-control mean difference at the declared query.

The complete generator, exact settings, selected query, seeds, analytical reference and independent numerical checks are available for agreed private review. Local generation, reproducibility and truth checks have passed. The proposed method comparison has not been run; scientific review and evaluation inclusion remain pending.

timeline.body:
Thanks for grounding this proposal in Rolling and Yang's Section 5.2 and documenting the fixed-query adaptation. Please push a new commit to this PR addressing the following items.

1. Move the proposal to `data-submissions/simulated-dgp/submissions/cate-rolling-yang-2014-gaussian-bump-v1.md`. The existing check reported “No data proposal changed” because the file was one directory above the submissions folder.
2. Add **Variables and data-generating process** from the [updated simulated DGP template](https://github.com/Statsinference/statsinference.github.io/blob/main/data-submissions/simulated-dgp/TEMPLATE.md). Define the observed columns and latent noise. Under **Structural equations**, give the distribution of the covariate and treatment, the assignment and error independence assumptions, and the outcome equation. Define both arm means and the Gaussian bump function explicitly so a reviewer can follow how the localized CATE arises. Please distinguish the source equations from any adaptations.
3. Write the reference estimand as `tau(u_star) = mu_1(u_star) - mu_0(u_star)` using the defined arm means. Please share the private review bundle with a maintainer, including the exact query and parameters, seeds, reference value, and one bounded command that generates an observed table and checks its truth. Keep protected evaluation settings in the private review materials.

A new commit on this PR is sufficient. Thank you.
